name: moku
description: Moku: the core toolkit plus one pack per moku framework. Install `moku`, then add the packs for the frameworks you use.

plugins.name: moku
plugins.description: The Moku Core toolkit: a conversational conductor that leads you from an idea through init, plan, build, verify and release, with strict lifecycle rails underneath, the vendored Moku Core specification, TDD build waves and a validation pipeline.

plugins.name: moku-web
plugins.description: @moku-labs/web pack: Preact islands, scoped CSS and tokens, the web validator, and real-browser e2e with exploratory QA and UX review.

plugins.name: moku-design
plugins.description: Design station for Moku: multi-round UI, API and architecture design that ends in a design context, plus GPT-6 Astra (through Codex) as artist and second opinion on user experience.

plugins.name: moku-worker
plugins.description: @moku-labs/worker pack: the Cloudflare Workers backend framework, with Durable Objects, Queues, R2, D1 and KV plugins.

plugins.name: moku-room
plugins.description: @moku-labs/room pack: couch multiplayer with a shared screen and phones, WebRTC state sync and QR join.

plugins.name: moku-native
plugins.description: @moku-labs/native pack: packages a Moku app as a Tauri 2 desktop or mobile app, with the permission surface generated from the composed system plugins.

plugins.name: moku-system
plugins.description: @moku-labs/system pack: one system API (store, notify, clipboard, tray, deep-link) that runs in the browser and in a Tauri shell behind a provider seam.

plugins.name: moku-common
plugins.description: @moku-labs/common pack: the shared logPlugin and envPlugin, env providers for Node, Cloudflare Workers and the browser, and the branded CLI kit.

plugins.name: moku-maintainer
plugins.description: Maintainer tools for the moku plugin repository itself: re-vendor the Moku Core spec and sync framework knowledge from upstream releases. Not needed to build with Moku.
